text: Introduction Renewable energy is really the generation of power in useful forms from natural sources such as the sun (solar energy), wind (air currents), water (hydro, waves, currents etc.), biological (biomass) and the earth itself (geothermal). This is an inexhaustible supply and technologies are evolving to make use of these processes for conversion to useable energy. The aim of these technologies is to provide sustainable energy production that is environmentally friendly. The program will account for both the development of renewable energy technologies and the efficient usage of conventional energy sources, while considering other societal and environmental aspects of energy development. Courses The following courses, worth five credits each, will be offered as required courses in the first semester: Renewable Energies, Energy Scenarios and Climate Protection Energy Technologies in Civil Engineering and Architecture Energy Technologies in Mechanical Engineering Material Science for Renewable Energy Systems Electrical Engineering and Information Technology Chemistry for Energy Scientists and Engineers Fundamental Law, Economics and Social Science Aspects of Energy Supply and Energy Consumption Students also have the opportunity to choose electives from offerings in the other sciences, law, humanities, languages, and more.
